name: SQLite SQL dialect
summary: The SQL dialect of the embedded SQLite library: a large subset of standard SQL with dynamic (per-value) typing, type affinity, a single-file database format and a bytecode virtual machine (VDBE) that every statement is compiled to.

level_notes.0: The canonical source lives in a Fossil repository at sqlite.org/src; github.com/sqlite/sqlite is the official read-only mirror linked here. The parser is generated by Lemon from src/parse.y; every statement is compiled to VDBE bytecode executed by src/vdbe.c.
level_notes.1: There is no specification separate from the implementation: the 'SQL As Understood By SQLite' pages on sqlite.org (with railroad syntax diagrams), the file-format document and the C-API reference are the normative description, and the test suites (TCL tests, sqllogictest, proprietary TH3) are the conformance evidence.
level_notes.2: sqlite.org itself publishes much of the best explanatory material (query planner, atomic commit, architecture); these are listed as level 2 guides/internals guides.
